subtitle: When Stone Learned to Share the Gods

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of temple complex under dawn sky
panels.action: Rudradeva stands before the rising triple-shrine of Hanamakonda, flanked by master stone craftsmen, as the star-shaped platform and clustered pillars emerge from the ground in pale dawn light.

dialogue.text: In Hanamakonda, between war and water, Rudradeva and his stone guilds dared a temple where Shiva, Vishnu and Surya shared one shining floor.

i18n.hi: युद्ध और जल के बीच हनमकोंडा में, रुद्रदेव और उसके शिल्पी एक मंदिर रचते हैं जहां शिव, विष्णु और सूर्य एक ही चमकते मंच पर साथ हैं।

panels.shot: slow push-in on inscription being carved
panels.action: A guild scribe and sculptor carve neat Telugu-Kannada letters into a stone slab, while Rudradeva watches, Warangal’s rocky landscape stretching behind him.

dialogue.text: In 1163, an inscription at Anumakonda named Rudradeva as ruler, fixing his sovereignty in stone while his mind turned to what new stone could yet do.

i18n.hi: ११६३ में, अनुमानकोंडा की शिला-लेख में रुद्रदेव को नरेश कहा गया, उसकी सत्ता पत्थर में दर्ज हुई, जबकि वह सोच रहा था कि पत्थर से अभी क्या नया हो सकता है।

panels.shot: wide documentary shot of Hanamakonda landscape with fort walls
panels.action: Rudradeva stands on a rocky outcrop above Hanamakonda, gesturing toward tanks, fort walls, and bustling markets as stone masons and surveyors mark lines on the ground.

dialogue.text: Around Hanamakonda, tanks, embankments and fort walls grew. For the Kakatiyas, stone was not only for gods, but for water, defense and rule.

i18n.hi: हनमकोंडा चारों ओर टैंक, बांध और किले की दीवारें उठती हैं। काकतीयों के लिए पत्थर सिर्फ देवताओं का नहीं, पानी, रक्षा और राज का भी है।

panels.shot: architectural top-down sketch shot over plans
panels.action: Guild architects sit on the floor with palm-leaf manuscripts and ground sketches, tracing a three-shrine plan on packed earth as Rudradeva leans forward, listening.

dialogue.text: From these stone-workers came a question: could one platform carry three shrines, three traditions, without fracture?

i18n.hi: इन्हीं शिल्पियों से सवाल उठता है: क्या एक ही मंच तीन मंदिर, तीन परंपराएँ बिना टूटे उठा सकता है?

panels.shot: medium shot circling around Rudradeva in council
panels.action: In a shaded hall, Rudradeva sits in council with Brahmins and guild leaders, a simple ground diagram showing three sanctums on a shared base between them.

dialogue.speaker: rudradeva_and_kakatiya_stone_guilds
dialogue.text: If my land has many paths to the divine, why must stone walk only one?

i18n.hi: जब मेरी भूमि में दिव्यता तक जाने कई राहें हैं, तो पत्थर एक ही राह क्यों चले?

panels.shot: dynamic low-angle of craftsmen at quarry
panels.action: Kakatiya stone workers at a hillside quarry strike large granite blocks free, dust hanging in the air, while an overseer holds a measuring cord and points toward Hanamakonda.

dialogue.text: Guilds mobilised. Quarries answered with great blocks. The planned trikutalayam needed stone that could bear both weight and meaning.

i18n.hi: संघ सक्रिय होते हैं। खदानें विशाल शिलाखंड भेजती हैं। जो त्रिकुटालयम सोचा गया, उसे ऐसे पत्थर चाहिए जो भार भी सहें, अर्थ भी।

panels.shot: architectural overhead of star-shaped foundation layout
panels.action: On the temple site, masons mark out a star-shaped plan with cords and pegs, the outline of a stellate platform emerging on the bare earth.

dialogue.text: Instead of a plain square, they traced a star. The platform itself would shift and turn, catching light differently at every hour.

i18n.hi: सीधे चौकोर के बजाय, वे एक तारा बनाते हैं। खुद मंच घूमता-सा है, हर घड़ी अलग रोशनी पकड़ता है।

panels.action: A craftsman leans over a carved stone pillar, rubbing its surface with abrasive sand and cloth until it gleams, his reflection faint on the smoothed stone.

dialogue.text: Their pillars were not lowly supports. They polished them until stone caught and returned a man’s face, as if the temple itself watched.

i18n.hi: ये स्तंभ बस सहारा नहीं। वे उन्हें इतना घिसते हैं कि पत्थर में आदमी का चेहरा लौट आए, जैसे खुद मंदिर देख रहा हो।

panels.shot: wide interior view of rising mandapa forest of columns
panels.action: Within the half-built mandapa, rows of intricately carved columns rise in different sizes and styles, craftsmen working at various levels like a forest taking shape.

dialogue.text: Later ages called it the Thousand Pillar Temple. The record shows many pillars, varied and deliberate, each speaking a different rhythm of craft.

i18n.hi: बाद के समय इसे ‘हज़ार स्तंभ मंदिर’ कहते हैं। अभिलेख बताते हैं अनेक स्तंभ, अलग-अलग सोच के, हर एक अपनी कारीगरी की ताल बोलता है।

panels.shot: medium shot of sculptors planning monolithic Nandi
panels.action: Senior sculptors sit around a massive single stone block marked with charcoal lines, the outline of a recumbent bull beginning to appear, as Rudradeva watches in quiet focus.

dialogue.text: From one stone, they planned Nandi, Shiva’s bull. Not assembled, but carved whole, a single mass made patient, powerful and alert.

i18n.hi: एक ही शिला से वे नंदी रचते हैं, शिव का वृषभ। जोड़ा नहीं जाता, पूरा एक ही पिंड, धैर्यवान, शक्तिशाली और सतर्क।

panels.shot: dramatic side view of Nandi partially carved
panels.action: The huge monolithic Nandi takes shape; its head and shoulders are carved, rest still rough, while a sculptor stands on scaffolding, chisel poised near the eye.

dialogue.speaker: rudradeva_and_kakatiya_stone_guilds
dialogue.text: When Nandi looks, let him look over all three shrines, not one alone.

i18n.hi: जब नंदी देखे, तो तीनों मंदिरों पर नज़र रखे, किसी एक पर नहीं।

panels.shot: sunlit wide shot of completed triple sanctums
panels.action: The three sanctums rise on the common star platform: central Shaiva shrine flanked by Vaishnava and Surya shrines, their shikharas distinct yet aligned under a clear sky.

dialogue.text: By the mid-1170s, the trikutalayam stood. Shiva, Vishnu and the Sun, three garbhagrihas sharing one carefully turned base.

i18n.hi: ११७० के दशक के मध्य तक त्रिकुटालयम खड़ा हो चुका है। शिव, विष्णु और सूर्य, तीन गर्भगृह एक ही सूझ-बूझ से घुमाए गए अधिष्ठान पर।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot showing different worshippers
panels.action: Inside the mandapa, different groups stand: one facing the Shiva linga, another before Vishnu’s image, a third offering water toward the Surya shrine, all under the same carved ceiling.

dialogue.text: In the cool hall, Shaiva, Vaishnava and Saura rites unfolded side by side. Shared pillars held prayers that did not sound the same.

i18n.hi: ठंडे मंडप में, शैव, वैष्णव और सौर पूजा साथ-साथ चलती है। साझा स्तंभ ऐसी प्रार्थनाएँ थामते हैं जो एक जैसी नहीं सुनाई देतीं।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of Rudradeva walking through mandapa
panels.action: Rudradeva walks slowly through the columned hall, touching a polished shaft as light from the doorway spills in, priests and guild elders watching from behind.

dialogue.text: For Rudradeva, this mandapa was more than piety. It displayed a kingdom where different devotions could stand under one carved roof.

i18n.hi: रुद्रदेव के लिए यह मंडप सिर्फ भक्ति नहीं। यह ऐसा राज्य दिखाता है जहां भिन्न उपासनाएँ एक ही नक्काशीदार छत के नीचे खड़ी रह सकती हैं।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide shot hinting at centuries passing
panels.action: The temple is shown in different seasons and subtle states of wear, trees growing and settlements changing around it, Nandi constant in the foreground.

dialogue.text: Centuries tested the stone. Weather, change of rulers, and neglect left scars, but the triple-shrine idea remained visible in the ground plan.

i18n.hi: सदियों ने पत्थर को परखा। मौसम, राज बदलना और उपेक्षा ने घाव दिए, पर जमीन के नक्शे में तीन-मंदिर की कल्पना अब भी साफ दिखती है।

panels.shot: modern documentary shot of ASI conservators at work
panels.action: In recent times, archaeologists and ASI conservators carefully reset dislodged pillars and reconstruct broken mandapa elements, modern tools lying beside traditional chisels.

dialogue.text: Modern conservation teams returned, guided by records and fragments, to stabilise the mandapa and recover as much of the Kakatiya design as time allowed.

i18n.hi: आधुनिक संरक्षण दल लौटते हैं, अभिलेख और टुकड़ों के सहारे, मंडप को स्थिर करने और जितना संभव हो सके काकतीया रूप फिर से उठाने।

panels.shot: wide shot linking Thousand Pillar Temple with Warangal Fort and Kala Thoranam
panels.action: A panoramic view connects Hanamakonda’s temple, Warangal Fort’s walls and the Kakatiya Kala Thoranam, all under the same horizon, with visitors walking among them.

dialogue.text: In UNESCO’s tentative list, Hanamakonda’s shrine sits with Warangal’s fort and Kala Thoranam, part of a serial story of Kakatiya stone, power and imagination.

i18n.hi: यूनेस्को की अस्थायी सूची में हनमकोंडा का मंदिर, वरंगल का किला और कला तोरणम साथ दर्ज हैं — काकतीया पत्थर, सत्ता और कल्पना की एक कड़ी कथा।

panels.shot: quiet close-up of Nandi facing the triple shrines at dusk
panels.action: At dusk, the monolithic Nandi rests in silhouette, looking toward the three sanctums as pilgrims move quietly, the polished pillars catching the last light.

dialogue.text: Hanamakonda’s three shrines remind us that difference need not mean distance: with care, one platform, one hall, one city can let many ways of worship stand together.

i18n.hi: हनमकोंडा के तीन मंदिर याद दिलाते हैं कि भिन्नता का मतलब दूरी नहीं होना चाहिए: संभाल से, एक ही मंच, एक ही मंडप, एक ही नगर में कई पूजा-पथ साथ खड़े रह सकते हैं।

subtitle_i18n.en: When Stone Learned to Share the Gods
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब पत्थर ने देवताओं को बांटना सीखा
